strings.name: Takashi Murakami
strings.summary: Murakami studied nihonga at Tokyo University of the Arts before developing a contemporary practice combining painting, sculpture, animation and merchandise. His Superflat theory examines Japanese visual traditions, postwar consumption and popular culture. He founded a production organization and supports other artists. Collaborations with fashion and music broadened his reach while prompting debate about art and commerce; his work has appeared in international museums.

strings.influence.rationale: Through Superflat theory and cross-disciplinary creation, he connects Japanese popular culture with contemporary art, influencing relationships among art, animation and commercial imagery.

strings.highlights.h1.title: Superflat theory
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses flat visual forms and popular imagery to examine Japanese artistic traditions and postwar culture.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Across media
strings.highlights.h2.text: Works between museums and commodity culture through painting, sculpture, animation and brand collaborations.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Cleveland exhibition
strings.timeline.t1.text: Presented a major exhibition at the Cleveland Museum of Art, showing work across media.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Versailles exhibition
strings.timeline.t2.text: Placed contemporary works in a historic palace, extending dialogue between art and cultural heritage.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Los Angeles retrospective
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Museum of Contemporary Art presented a retrospective that later toured other international institutions.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Louis Vuitton collaboration
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began working with the brand, applying his visual language to fashion and merchandise.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Establishes Kaikai Kiki
strings.timeline.t5.text: Developed his earlier production studio into a company organizing art production and support for artists.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Introduces Superflat
strings.timeline.t6.text: Used exhibitions and publishing to articulate Superflat, linking visual traditions and contemporary popular culture.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Creates Hiropon Factory
strings.timeline.t7.text: Established a production studio that laid foundations for later team-based art production.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned a nihonga doctorate at Tokyo University of the Arts, then expanded his contemporary art activities.
